summary: src/lib/cost.ts: computeCost(modelId, inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedTokens, at) with model_pricing lookup; tests
description:
src/lib/cost.ts — computes cost_usd for a request.

  export async function computeCost(args: {
    modelId: string;
    inputTokens: number;
    outputTokens: number;
    cachedInputTokens?: number;
    at?: Date;  // defaults to now
  }): Promise<{ cost_usd: number; pricing: ModelPricing }>;

Pricing lookup: SELECT … FROM model_pricing WHERE model_id = $1 AND effective_from <= $2 AND (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to > $2) ORDER BY effective_from DESC LIMIT 1.

Cost formula:
  fresh_input = inputTokens - cachedInputTokens
  cost = fresh_input * input_price / 1_000_000
       + cachedInputTokens * (cached_input_price ?? input_price) / 1_000_000
       + outputTokens * output_price / 1_000_000

If pricing row not found, throw — don't silently default to 0 (better to fail loudly than under-charge silently).

Tests (table-driven):
- DeepSeek query, no caching: input + output cost matches manual calc
- Sonnet query, no caching: same
- Sonnet query with cached_input: cache pricing applied to cached portion only
- Unknown model: throws
- Pricing change mid-stream (effective_from/to boundaries): correct row picked by 'at'

Done when:
- src/lib/cost.ts exports computeCost with the signature above
- src/__tests__/cost.test.ts covers the cases above
- All existing tests still pass
